blocks.text: The Docker socket is the full Docker API, and that API can start a privileged container with the host filesystem mounted, so any container with the socket mounted is host root once compromised.

blocks.code:
volumes:
  - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock     # dashboards, Traefik discovery, CI runners

blocks.text: `:ro` doesn't help: it only restricts filesystem operations on the socket file. API calls, including "create privileged container", still work.

rows: No socket needed (e.g., Traefik file provider)
Expose only needed GET endpoints; block create/exec
Blast radius = the unprivileged daemon user
Ephemeral VMs / daemonless builders for CI

blocks.text: In reviews, grep every compose file for `docker.sock` and `privileged: true`. Each hit needs a written justification or a replacement.

Q: "Is mounting docker.sock read-only safe?" A: "No. :ro only affects file operations on the socket; the API is still fully usable, including creating a privileged container that mounts /. Treat socket access as root and use a filtering proxy, static configuration or rootless mode."

items: Filter, avoid or de-privilege the daemon.
Audit compose files for socket mounts.
